There are a few problems to be resolved but eventually we will get there.

The most immediate problem seems to be the landing and secure latching to an asteroid. Philae was the first to try such a thing and demonstrated that it is not as easy as we thought it would be. We need to develop means to securely latch ourselves to the asteroid.

The second problem is the actual mining. We only know about mining in Earth gravity ant that only on large scale and with huge workforce to operate and maintain the equipment. We need to figure out how to do mining without human participation and without maintenance, in zero gravity. Obviously any technology developed to achieve this will be applied to mining on Earth as well.

Third problem to overcome is ISRU - In Situ Resource Utilization. There are only a few things which are valuable enough to send back to Earth. Some heavy metals like gold platinum osmium etc. are valuable enough to send back, everything else is much more valuable in orbit. So we need to figure out how to make use of the mined material in orbit. How do you manufacture a sheet of steel so you can use it to build a habitat? This question will have to be answered.
It gets more complicated too. Many metals develop an oxidized layer in our atmosphere that would be absent in space, causing two such pieces to weld together just by touch.
